text:
maria: Quick sync — I'm changing the async job endpoint behavior for cancel and stale poll tokens. Need quick opinions on backward compatibility + what to return for in-flight cancels. TL;DR: prefer 200 + status body instead of 202+empty for compatibility with JS clients. :thinking:

kevin: Can you sketch the current vs new shapes? helps to visualise tradeoffs.

maria: Current (old clients expect):
```json
{
  "status": "pending" | "running" | "completed",
  "result_url": null | "/jobs/:id/result"
}
```
New proposal: include cancel/error metadata and a token TTL field so pollers can stop earlier:
```json
{
  "status": "pending" | "running" | "completed" | "cancelled",
  "progress_pct": 0-100,
  "result_url": null | string,
  "cancel_reason": null | string,
  "poll_token_ttl_secs": 30,
  "last_updated": "2025-10-02T12:34:56Z"
}
```

maria: Behavior: if client posts a cancel -> server marks job "cancelling" and returns current status (200) with cancel_reason set when observed. Poll calls always return a 200 + JSON status shape. We will avoid returning 202 with empty body because our frontend polling lib assumes a body parse.

anna: I like always-200 for poll GETs. But how do we signal that a cancel request was accepted but not yet applied? "cancelling" vs "cancelled" distinction?

maria: Good call. Proposed states: pending -> running -> cancelling -> cancelled OR completed. So pollers see "cancelling" and can stop polling aggressively after X tries. We'll also set poll_token_ttl_secs to min(remaining_grace, default) so clients don't hammer.

kevin: How do old clients handle the extra fields? They only read top-level status and ignore others. So that's fine. Edge case: old clients that treat unknown statuses as terminal might break if they see "cancelling". Should we instead map "cancelling" -> "running" for backward compatibility, and include a hint field?

maria: Option A: keep new status values and add a compat_status top-level string for legacy consumers:
```json
{
  "status": "cancelling",
  "compat_status": "running"
}
```
Option B: keep only legacy values but add detail object with lifecycle_reason. Which do folks prefer?

tim: Prefer Option A. Explicit > implicit. Add `compat_status` so older clients keep working and new clients can be precise. We should document it in the SDKs.

lucy: For cancel request response code: POST /jobs/:id/cancel should return 202 if accepted for asynchronous cancellation, or 200 if immediate? We need to be consistent. Our SDK currently expects 200 and reads a status body.

maria: Agree. Let's always return 200 with the job status body on cancel endpoints too. That keeps client flow uniform: POST /cancel -> 200 + status; GET /status -> 200 + status. We risk hiding that the operation is async, but status will indicate "cancelling" and `poll_token_ttl_secs` tells them when to stop polling or switch to exponential backoff.

kevin: We should add a header to help intermediate clients: `X-Job-Operation: cancel; async=true` and maybe `Retry-After` when we want clients to delay. That avoids changing HTTP semantics.

maria: Good call. Plan:
- Always return 200 for status and cancel endpoints with the full status JSON.
- Add `compat_status` for old clients.
- Add `X-Job-Operation` header on cancel responses and `Retry-After` if we want explicit wait.
- Set `poll_token_ttl_secs` to ~30s by default, configurable per-customer.

anna: How should the SDK interpret poll_token_ttl_secs? stop polling after TTL expires even if job still running? That could lose job end events.

maria: SDK behavior: treat TTL as a hint. After TTL expires, switch to exponential backoff (e.g., 1s -> 2s -> 4s) up to a max interval. Not stop entirely. We want to reduce load, not drop observation.

ops-bot: deploy-check: new status enum must be added to schema validators and feature flag rollout for 2 weeks to watch for client breakage. :rotating_light: 

lucy: What about long-poll/streaming endpoints? Some consumers use SSE to avoid polling. We should ensure SSE messages use same status schema.

maria: Yes, SSE payload will mirror the same JSON. For SSE we'll send an event `job.status` with the status body. That keeps surface area consistent.

tim: Tests: add contract tests that deserialise to both legacy model (status string) and new model (full object). Add integration test where cancel request returns:
```bash
curl -X POST /jobs/abc123/cancel -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
```
Expect body includes `status="cancelling"` and `compat_status="running"`.

kevin: Also add a quick migration note for Dedicated/private customers who run older SDKs—might need a minor SDK bump to honour `compat_status` mapping. Put this in the changelog.

maria: Action items:
- @kevin: PR for schema + compat_status header + unit tests (ETA: EOD Weds)
- @anna: update SDK poller logic to respect `poll_token_ttl_secs` as hint and `compat_status` fallback (ETA: Thurs)
- @tim: add integration test for cancel race & Retry-After semantics (ETA: Thurs)
- @lucy: docs + console note about observing cancelling vs cancelled (ETA: Fri)
- ops-bot: feature flag rollout for 2 weeks and telemetry capture for unknown statuses

anna: acked. I'll start SDK patch now.

kevin: I'll open PR and link this thread.

maria: thanks team. If no objections by EOD I'll merge the schema change behind a feature flag. :thumbsup: 

lucy: +1

ops-bot: recorded action items and scheduled rollout window.
